name: Pois Green
lede: Pois Green is a muted, grayish yellow-green recorded by Ridgway in 1912 and filed in ColorHub's data under pois, the French word for pea.

sections.title: A pea-colored green
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 nomenclature places this hue at plate XLI, hue 29''', tone i, and the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 files it as block 122, a grayish yellow green [1]. Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary gives a first recorded date of 1905, at plate 22 G 5 [1]. ColorHub's library tags the name to the word pois, French for pea, but nothing in our sources confirms that link directly, so the exact derivation stays undocumented here [2].

The nearest named color is [[celadon-green|Celadon Green]], 4.2 units away and a touch cooler; [[chromium-green|Chromium Green]] sits 4.3 units off, slightly yellower [2]. [[reed-green|Reed Green]], a darker olive carrying the same reed word elsewhere in this family, is 5.7 units away [2]. In LCH terms Pois Green measures lightness 56, chroma 20, hue 119 degrees [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds Pois Green in 663 of 23,781 paintings, 2.79 percent, as photographed, more common than 80 percent of the archive's named colors [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 68 of 1,674 paintings, at 2.5 times the expected rate, and Peter Snayers is its most devoted painter, present in 4 of his 16 works here at 5.8 times his baseline [3]. It most often turns up as a hidden color, tucked into shadow, in 31 percent of its paintings [3]. The earliest match is dated 916, nine hundred ninety-six years before Ridgway's 1912 record of the name — a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not proof of a pea-green pigment, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3].
